articles.title: The promise and peril of AI in government
articles.summary:
In Taoyuan, Taiwan’s bustling industrial hub where 200 semiconductor manufacturing facilities are based, Mayor San-Cheng Chang is using AI to orchestrate an ambitious transformation. He brings a unique blend of technical expertise and government experience to the challenge of running the country’s fastest-growing city. Before becoming mayor, he served as Taiwan’s first nonpartisan premier and held leadership positions at both Google and Acer. As a former director of Taiwan’s National Center for High-Performance Computing, Chang embodies the intersection of technology and governance that helps explain Taoyuan’s embrace of AI.
As the home of Taiwan’s international airport as well as 2.2 million residents, Taoyuan must manage heavy truck traffic, air pollution, rapid population growth, and constant construction. Since March 2023, Taoyuan has run an AI-powered lung cancer screening initiative targeting citizens over 40 with risk factors that include occupational exposure and family history. Two years later, Taoyuan’s program had screened over 400,000 residents, detecting 233 lung cancer cases (90% in early stage), and achieving cost savings of NT$500 million ($17 million) through AI-aided diagnostics. To manage this volume without overwhelming local hospitals, the city deployed advanced AI software, which can predict cancer risk from a single low-dose CT scan without requiring additional clinical data, helping doctors to efficiently triage cases and focus resources on those most …

articles.title: Google Wallet can finally unlock doors with digital home keys
articles.summary:
Google has added digital home key support to Google Wallet, allowing Android users to open smart locks by tapping their phone against them or simply approaching. The feature is currently available in public preview for the Google Home app, and will roll out to everyone “over the coming weeks,” according to Google’s announcement.
Google Wallet can finally unlock doors with digital home keys
Android users can add digital keys for compatible smart locks in Google Home to their Wallet app.
This was a long time coming, given Samsung and Apple users have had this convenience for a while now. While Google Home already has some unlocking functionality, this update allows users to leverage the Near Field Communication (NFC) and Ultra-Wideband (UWB) tech in their phones with compatible smart locks. Multiple locks can be controlled via Google Wallet using a single digital home key. All household members linked to the same Google Home account can also add their own key to their personal Google Wallet.
Tap to Unlock works by holding the back of an NFC-enabled Android phone near the lock reader, and doesn’t require the phone to be unlocked. Unlock on Approach needs to be manually enabled in Google Wallet, but can automatically unlock a door when it detects the user walking up.

articles.title: Los modelos de IA ahora tienen una vida media de solo 6 semanas: esta es la causa
articles.summary:
El tiempo que los equipos de desarrollo dedican a cada modelo de inteligencia artificial se reduce de forma acelerada. Según el informe AI Gateway Production Index de noviembre de 2026, elaborado por Vercel, los equipos que pagan por servicios de IA permanecen con un modelo nuevo durante un promedio de cuatro semanas antes de migrar hacia otra alternativa recién lanzada. El objetivo detrás de este recambio constante es mantener competitivo el desarrollo de código o de agentes basados en IA.
El reporte sostiene que esta dinámica revela que los modelos de inteligencia artificial tienen, en la práctica, una vida media de aproximadamente seis semanas. Pasado ese período, la atención y el uso del modelo disminuyen a medida que desarrolladores y equipos adoptan la siguiente opción disponible en el mercado.
La adopción ocurre en cuestión de días
El análisis sobre las transacciones de tokens que circulan por su plataforma muestra que los equipos comienzan a usar modelos nuevos apenas días después de su lanzamiento. Esta velocidad se explica porque apuntar un entorno de desarrollo o un editor de código hacia un modelo distinto resulta, en general, un proceso sencillo cuando se emplean herramientas de integración o “wrappers”.
Vercel desglosa la adopción en tres franjas temporales: de 0 a 14 días, de 15 a 30 días y de 31 a 60 días desde el lanzamiento. Los datos muestran una tendencia creciente hacia la adopción temprana desde junio de 2026. Para septiembre, casi el 17% de los usuarios…

articles.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft Amid $5 Million Extortion Attempt
articles.summary:
Shipping giant Maersk has confirmed that hackers extracted data from one of its IT systems, while an extortion group claims to have stolen sensitive information and is demanding $5 million.
In a November 11 statement, the Danish company said the affected system was inherited through an earlier acquisition. Maersk has not identified the acquired business.
The company said its cybersecurity team discovered the intrusion and launched an investigation, with action being taken to secure the affected system.
“Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed,” Maersk said.
“The incident is isolated to a local system,” the company added, saying it had found no indication of an impact on other Maersk systems or on customer and partner systems connected through APIs and EDI.
Maersk does not anticipate disruptions to customer operations and says its shipping platforms remain available for booking and managing shipments.
The disclosure follows a claim by the WhiteArmor ransomware group, which listed Maersk on its leak site on November 7 and threatened to publish stolen information unless a $5 million ransom is paid.
WhiteArmor claims to have obtained approximately 100GB of data from a platform associated with LF Logistics, a Hong Kong-based logistics company acquired by Maersk in 2022.
The alleged haul includes roughly 29,000 driver records, of which 16,093 contain plaintext passwords, and 16,123 staff accounts, including 33 with superadministrator privileges.

L’acteur de 43 ans faisait la promotion de Mustache Protocol, un jeu vidéo rétro façon années 80 qu’il a conçu avec Google, à l’aide des outils d’IA de son nouvel ordinateur portable, le Googlebook. Mais la discussion a rapidement basculé sur son avenir chez DC et son rôle de Superman.
Henry Cavill dans Superman ?
Le journaliste d’Inverse lui a demandé s’il reprendrait la cape, par exemple dans la peau du Superman vieillissant de la bande dessinée Kingdom Come. Henry Cavill a répondu en citant le dessin animé Fievel et le Nouveau Monde :
« Écoutez, il y a énormément d’histoires fantastiques. Il y a toujours beaucoup d’opportunités. Comme le chantait le pigeon à Fievel dans Fievel et le Nouveau Monde : “il ne faut jamais dire jamais”. Et j’adhère à ça. J’ai passé des moments tellement merveilleux à jouer Superman par le passé. Je ne dirais jamais jamais maintenant. »
En décembre 2022, moins de deux mois après avoir annoncé son retour à la suite de son caméo dans Black Adam, Henry Cavill avait dû faire ses adieux au rôle. articles.title: More game developers are starting to use generative AI
articles.summary:
More video game developers are using generative AI tools in their jobs compared to last year, according to the GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey. Forty percent of developers surveyed say they use it “as part of their job,” an increase from 36 percent in 2025. Usage was higher with game developers that work on free-to-play games at 58 percent and mobile-only studio workers at 70 percent.
More game developers are starting to use generative AI
The GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey shows an increase in AI usage among game developers.
The survey is being published as the game industry continues to reckon with generative AI tools. While many game developers, particularly indie developers, have spoken out strongly against the technology, AI is at the center of indie awards conversations in part because Big Walk developer House House “sparingly” used LLMs to assist with technical challenges in the “final stretch” of development. AI is also increasingly being used to reverse-engineer retro games. And in a post on Thursday, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma seemed to indicate that AI will be central to Xbox’s future, saying that “A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars.”
Seventy three percent of the survey’s respondents said they used AI for research and brainstorming, while 62 percent used it for data analysis and summarization, and 56 percent for code generation and debugging. …

O que é a CoreWeave e por que ela importa para a IA?
A CoreWeave é uma provedora de computação em nuvem especializada em oferecer capacidade de processamento para aplicações de inteligência artificial. Seu negócio está ligado à expansão de empresas que precisam de grandes volumes de recursos computacionais para desenvolver e executar essas tecnologias.
A companhia faz parte do grupo conhecido como neoclouds. Diferentemente de gigantes como Alphabet, Amazon e Microsoft, essas empresas são mais jovens e concentram sua atuação no fornecimento de infraestrutura computacional. Elas não precisam desenvolver seus próprios modelos de IA para participar desse mercado: podem atender desenvolvedores e companhias que trabalham com essas tecnologias.
Nesse papel, a CoreWeave atua como parceira independente de empresas como Anthropic e OpenAI, além de competir com os grandes provedores de nuvem. Sua relevância está justamente em fornecer capacidade computacional para um setor cuja expansão exige cada vez mai…

articles.title: Mangaluru’s Zupple Labs wins DRDO’s first-ever blockchain defence project
articles.summary:
Mangaluru’s Zupple Labs wins DRDO’s first-ever blockchain defence project
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs is the first blockchain startup selected under DRDO’s Technology Development Fund. Over 30 months, it will build an indigenous security-audit framework for defence applications.
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs has been selected by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) under its Technology Development Fund (TDF) programme. Its brief: build India's first indigenous framework for security auditing of blockchain applications in the defence sector.
The selection is rare by any measure. Fewer than 90 projects have made it through the TDF programme in its ten-year history, and this is the first in the blockchain domain.
What DRDO has asked Zupple Labs to build
Over the next 30 months, Zupple Labs will develop a platform that DRDO will use to standardise security audits of upcoming blockchain applications across the defence sector.
As defence agencies explore distributed ledgers for records, logistics and authentication, a common auditing standard matters. It gives every new application the same security bar before deployment, and keeps that capability built and owned in India.
Trust infrastructure for governments
Zupple Labs builds blockchain-powered trust infrastructure for governments and institutions, with a presence across four countries. Its systems secure and authenticate critical citizen records, making them tamper-evident and verifiable.

articles.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
articles.summary:
Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found.
AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
A study testing Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT found that in as many as 15 percent of conversations, chatbots displayed ‘risky’ URLs.
The study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi and shared exclusively with The Verge prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of 151 brands. Questions included “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?”; “Where can I find [brand] online?”; and “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?” The test ran over the course of two testing periods in September and asked about 151 small and large companies like fashion brands Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, and Madhappy (a client of Podqi) and homeware brand Le Creuset. Podqi crafted its own prompts (as opposed to using real user conversations) and tested its prompts using a tool that tracks AI answers across chatbots.
Perplexity performed the worst, showing risky sites in 15 percent of answers
Over the course of 6,795 answers, Podqi found that all three AI engines cited and showed shoppers risky sites, defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, old brand domains that have been reregistered by someone else, or dead sites that aren’t active at all but that someone…

A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay could allow attackers to access private container images and replace content in repositories across an affected registry.
Red Hat Quay is an enterprise container registry used to store, manage and distribute container images. It allows organizations to control who can download or upload images used in application development and deployment.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123710, has a CVSS score of 9.8. It affects deployments where the service responsible for managing signing keys is accessible to untrusted clients.
“This Critical flaw in Red Hat Quay’s service key server allows an unauthenticated attacker to take over registry token signing,” Red Hat said in its advisory.
When anonymous access is enabled, an attacker without an account can obtain a registry token and exploit weaknesses in the key rotation mechanism to install their own trusted signing key.
The attacker can then generate tokens granting read and write access to any repository, bypassing normal access restrictions. This could expose private images and any credentials or other secrets stored in them, while also allowing attackers to overwrite images that other systems subsequently download.
The malicious signing key can be configured without an expiration date and survives registry restarts unless removed.
“Rotation also deletes the legitimate instance key as a side effect, and the attacker key can delete replacement instance keys,” Red Hat’s Bugzilla report expl…

A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.

- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. At OCP Summit 2026, we saw Meta’s new MetaRoCE network adapter. This is Meta’s answer to providing an open RDMA transport layer that has features like packet spraying, congestion control, and more. This was a presentation we saw at OCP Summit, but Meta had a NIC on display.
Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter at OCP 2026
Here is the display from the Meta booth at OCP Summit 2026, where you can see an OCP NIC 3.0 card.
During its OCP 2026 presentation, Meta shared some of the big features of MetaRoCE:
- Per-path reliability and congestion control
- Receiver rate hints (RCN) for fast incast convergence
- Tolerates packet loss and reordering
- Single QP carries multiple streams over multiple network paths
- Runs on commodity Ethernet: ECN + ECMP, no switch (Source: Meta)
Before OCP Summit, Meta demonstrated this with the AMD Pensando NIC series. The programmability allowed it to implement the protocol without having dedicated hardware. That allows Meta to potentially source from multiple vendors.
Meta is trying to build a network protocol that can scale to million-GPU training, but also that can run on different network topologies and hardware.

articles.title: Foundation IP For The AI Era: Why Execution Shapes SoC Cost ─ eBook
articles.summary:
How an integrated foundation IP strategy can reduce execution risk, enable faster tape-out, and lower TCO.
As AI workloads push power, performance, voltage, and process variation to new limits, the economics of advanced-node SoCs are changing. In addition to the cost of the IP itself, hidden costs often arrive later in the design cycle: integration delays, schedule slips, re-spins, and missed market windows. As design complexity rises, predictable execution is becoming a critical factor in total cost of ownership (TCO) alongside power, performance, and area (PPA).
Sourcing Foundation IP piece by piece can add another layer of complexity. Logic libraries, embedded memories, I/Os, and OTP NVM IP from multiple suppliers bring different deliverables, roadmaps, support models, and integration requirements. An integrated Foundation IP platform can reduce these seams by bringing the core building blocks together as one silicon-proven, verified stack, with sign-off-ready characterization and IP + EDA co-optimization to improve PPA and accelerate implementation. This tighter alignment helps design teams move toward tape-out with greater predictability.
The impact extends beyond integration. Across HPC and Edge AI designs, improvements in PPA can translate into meaningful economic value through smaller die area, lower operating power, and increased performance, while avoiding a re-spin or major tape-out delay can protect even more value. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.summary:
Microsoft has spent the past 25 years trying to shake up the game console market. The original Xbox, which launched on November 15th in 2001, took on an industry dominated by Sony and Nintendo. Twenty-five years later, Xbox finds itself in a similar position. It’s not starting from scratch this time around, but to reach another 25-year milestone, it needs to do something radically different.
25 years later, Xbox is trying to reinvent itself again
Xbox has always been about trying something new, so what does Microsoft do next?

articles.title: Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
articles.summary:
Multiple threat actors are abusing GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, to maintain access to Linux servers even after patching the vulnerabilities exploited to gain initial access.
Since March, detections of malicious GSocket activity have increased, particularly in attacks targeting web applications and hosting environments.
GSocket allows attackers to reach systems behind firewalls or NAT by intercepting network connections and replacing the program's conventional IP-layer communication with its own transport layer, which routes traffic through the Global Socket Relay Network.
Since both endpoints initiate outbound connections to the relay, which matches them and brokers an end-to-end encrypted session, an attacker can reconnect without needing the compromised server's IP address or hostname.
This makes it more difficult for defenders to disrupt attacks using IP- or domain-based access control lists.
According to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint telemetry, GSocket-related detections increased by 356.2% between March and August.
Microsoft explains that both the compromised server and the attacker connect outbound, hence the server needs no inbound listener implants, making the attack stealthier.
“The compromised host and the operator both connect outbound to the relay, which bridges the two sessions,” Microsoft explains.
“The host needs no inbound listener or public IP address, and network address translation does not prevent the connection.”

articles.title: Hackers Deploy Malware in Fresh ScreenConnect Campaign
articles.summary:
A threat actor has compromised hundreds of endpoints across dozens of ConnectWise ScreenConnect customers in a fresh campaign, cybersecurity outfit Huntress reports.
The attacks were observed on November 11, when the hackers abused their unauthorized access to cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to run commands on managed endpoints.
According to Huntress, the campaign compromised at least 6 MSPs and 288 hosts across 48 organizations. The attackers hit all 288 compromised hosts within 90 minutes.
The attackers’ commands deployed rogue ScreenConnect clients and a malware toolkit called SCKit that provides persistent backdoor access, intercepts session cookies, and can self-replicate.
Initially deployed via ScreenConnect panels, it waits for a technician to connect to the compromised endpoint to infect their workstation. Next, attempts to compromise other sessions the technician has access to and spread itself to other panels.

articles.title: Por que os jogos demoram tanto para chegar ao Nintendo Switch 2?

No dia 19 de novembro, GTA 6 chega ao PlayStation 5 e ao Xbox Series X|S. Não chega ao Nintendo Switch 2 — e apesar dos boatos… a Rockstar nunca disse se um dia vai chegar.
A cena é velha conhecida de quem joga no console da Nintendo. Doom levou cerca de um ano e meio para sair no Switch original. The Witcher 3 levou quatro anos e meio. Cyberpunk 2077 só desembarcou na plataforma em 2025, quase cinco anos depois da estreia nos outros consoles. E mesmo agora, com o Switch 2 já há um ano e meio no mercado, a história continua se repetindo: 007 First Light foi adiado três vezes e agora só sai em março de 2027.
A explicação fácil é a potência. O Switch 2 é mais fraco que um PS5, logo os jogos precisam ser reduzidos, sofrer adaptações e isso demora. Só que a explicação fácil está incompleta. Os atrasos têm pelo menos quatro causas, a mais decisiva delas não tem nada a ver com gráficos: tem a ver com conseguir o aparelho para programar.
O Switch 2 é fraco demais para jogos AAA?
O problema técnico do Switch 2 não é exatamente “ser fraco”. É ser estreito.
Segundo o levantamento da Digital Foundry, o console usa um chip Nvidia T239 customizado, com 12 GB de memória LPDDR5X e GPU de 1.536 núcleos CUDA. A largura de banda de memória é de 102 GB/s no modo dock e cai para 68 GB/s no modo portátil. Para efeito de comparação, o PS5 trabalha com cerca de 448 GB/s e o Xbox Series X com algo perto de 560 GB/s.

articles.title: Introduction To FP8 Formats: Part 1
articles.summary:
The rationale behind 8-bit floating-point data formats, their ecosystem momentum, and hardware support.
The industry is moving from high-precision formats (FP32, FP16, BF16) to lower-precision data types for Machine Learning (ML) inference and training. In cloud and data center environments, lower-precision data types deliver higher throughput by packing more compute per cycle from the same platform. On edge and mobile devices, smaller formats reduce model size, memory footprint and bandwidth, which directly affects power consumption and latency.
Arm, Intel, and NVIDIA published an OCP 8-bit Floating Point Specification (OFP8). It is an interchange format that allows software systems to share the models easily. FP8 is not a future concept, it is being deployed today. It is already supported by NVIDIA’s Hopper H100 GPU, with software deployment appearing in major ML frameworks.
Arm added the FP8 support to the Arm v9 ISA and is exploring the best way to integrate the FP8 across all the ML platforms.
This blog post explains the FP8 data formats, the new Floating-point Mode Register (FPMR), and the instruction set that makes FP8 practical on Arm CPUs.
Unlike IEEE FP64, FP32, and FP16, FP8 is not a single format, it is a family. The whitepaper FP8 Formats for Deep Learning proposes an FP8 format consisting of two encodings: E4M3 and E5M2.
With only 8 bits available, FP8 makes a trade-off between precision and dynamic range. A single encoding cannot fit all tensors equally well. A…

Un reset pour toutes les limites des abonnements payants
Via son compte X ClaudeDevs, Anthropic a annoncé une réinitialisation complète et gratuite des limites d’utilisation pour les abonnés Pro, Max, Ultra et Team. Anthropic explique avoir décidé d’offrir ce reset des comptes payants pour deux raisons. Premièrement, l’entreprise américaine confie avoir corrigé récemment quelques « petits problèmes qui consommaient plus de limites que prévu », sans préciser lesquels. Deuxièmement, Anthropic reconnaît en quelque sorte que le reset offert le 9 novembre, à l’occasion du lancement de Claude Fable 5.2, n’a pas réellement profité aux abonnés qui avaient déjà atteint leurs limites hebdomadaires. articles.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
articles.summary:
Microsoft has confirmed that Windows updates released since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday are causing SQL Server performance and stability issues.
As detailed in a Windows release health dashboard update on Wednesday, this is caused by server queries that leave connections open after the queries complete. These connections accumulate instead of closing, degrading server performance over time.
"This issue affects SQL Server linked server queries that use OLE DB providers to connect to external databases. Oracle and PostgreSQL connections are among those known to be affected," Microsoft explained.
"In affected environments, administrators might observe an increasing number of open connections to external databases, even when the associated SQL Server linked server queries are no longer running."
It also added that admins may be able to manually close connections left open due to this bug or restart the SQL service to temporarily address stability and performance issues, but this can also kill active queries and may not fully address the issue, as it will resurface again after some time.
Microsoft says the issues impact both client (Windows 10 and Windows 11) and server (Windows Server 2012 and later) systems and will be fixed with an out-of-band Windows update to be released over the next few days.
While it works to resolve the bug, Microsoft said IT administrators can reach out to Microsoft Support for Business for a mitigation that can address the issue until a fix is availa…

articles.title: Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones
Penlink’s Webloc is an application that locates people using information from the weather, gaming, email, and religious apps on their phone. It’s sold to the police.
The tool collects vast quantities of location data from smartphones via commonly used weather, gaming, email and religious apps. It can build a detailed picture of where a smartphone has been over the past 12 months, and update the data hourly, showing the movements of people on a near real-time basis. Law enforcement officers can use Webloc to zero in on a map and look at all phones that were present at a specific place and time, analyzing “billions of location data points,” according to company documents reviewed by Bloomberg.
There’s a nice infographic that explains how the system works at the link.
Rontea • November 12, 2026 9:20 AM

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned
articles.summary:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis.
The 63-year-old will be replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim chief executive.
His exit comes after he admitted to having a relationship with a woman that US authorities believe was a Chinese spy. It also emerged on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive.
Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in pre-market trading, extending earlier losses after the announcement of Huang’s resignation.
Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, led it to become what was until recently the world’s most valuable company.
Huang’s departure marks a startling end to his more than 33-year tenure, during which Nvidia evolved from a small video-game chip company into the linchpin of the global AI infrastructure boom.
Huang has become one of the most recognizable figures in tech, as Nvidia’s semiconductors became integral to training and running AI systems such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude.
Nvidia stock extended its pre-market decline after the company announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive.
Shares were down 10.2 percent in pre-market trading, a move that would wipe off more than $400 billion in market capitalization.
This story was updated on November 12 with news of Huang’s resignation.

articles.title: Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch
articles.summary:
“Fifty-seven channels, and nothin’ on.”
Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.
Within a few years, there would be hundreds of TV channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch.”
The advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.
According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.
Gracenote, a Nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the UK who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 State of Play: Amid fragmentation frustrations, UX is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.
For example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch.”

articles.title: Northside Ventures aims to build “institutional angel investor” with $30-million USD second fund | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Toronto-based Northside Ventures has officially launched its second venture capital (VC) fund geared towards Canadian technology founders at the earliest stages of company formation.
Northside aims to raise $30 million USD ($40 million CAD) for Fund II by early 2027. The firm is already more than halfway there, having secured $17 million USD ($24 million CAD) in total commitments to date across two closes, surpassing the size of its inaugural $11-million USD ($15 million CAD) fund.
“We’re taking the approach of being an institutional angel investor in the Canadian ecosystem.”
Northside founder and solo general partner (GP) Alex McIsaac revealed the news in an exclusive interview with BetaKit. While the firm’s overall strategy remains largely to continue its focus on pre-seed Canadian tech startups at or near inception, Northside hopes to cut bigger cheques and invest in companies with a larger second fund.
Through Fund II, Northside intends to deploy an average of $500,000 USD into each startup’s first round of financing, which is more than twice as much as the $225,000 it deployed via Fund I. It also plans to double its reserves for follow-on investments in top-performing firms to 20 percent, and invest in a total of 40 companies (10 more than its predecessor).

articles.title: Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack
articles.summary:
All-in-one collaborative workspace and productivity platform Notion is notifying a small set of customers that their information was compromised in a data breach involving Fireworks AI.
A cloud platform for running and fine-tuning open source AI models, Fireworks AI was hacked twice in October: once through compromised internal credentials, and once through a third-party cloud provider that was hosting Fireworks R&D machines.
The second incident, linked to a recent rise in LLMJacking activity, occurred on October 24, when the attackers executed an unauthorized workload leading to the compromise of customer data.
Fireworks contained the incident the same day and notified Notion on November 2 that Notion AI data had been accessed. Prior to the incident, Notion used Fireworks as a general inference provider for delivering open-weight models.
Notion’s investigation into the compromised data determined that the hackers accessed Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, which helps customers understand their AI usage.
Fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces were affected, and most of the transcripts were unattributable to a customer or the workspace they came from.
“Beyond what’s in the chat transcript itself, there’s no information tying the chat back to workspaces, users or companies,” Notion says.

articles.title: Los sindicatos australianos acusan a grandes empresas de usar la IA para justificar despidos
articles.summary:
Sindicatos y expertos de Australia acusan a grandes empresas del país de usar la inteligencia artificial como justificación para recortar empleos y trasladar trabajo al exterior, según informó la agencia Reuters. La práctica tiene nombre en inglés, AI washing: atribuir despidos a la IA cuando la causa principal es el ahorro de costos.
El caso que encendió el debate es el de Qantas. La aerolínea nacional anunció el 10 de noviembre que eliminará 850 empleos y trasladará al exterior algunas funciones corporativas, como parte de una reorganización con la consultora Accenture que se apoya en la IA.
La aerolínea respondió que seguirá consultando a los sindicatos y que se concentra en ofrecer a los afectados otros puestos dentro de la empresa y apoyo. No contestó a la acusación de AI washing, según Reuters.
No es la única compañía señalada. Las empresas de software WiseTech y Atlassian recortaron personal este año y atribuyeron los despidos a la IA. La telefónica Telstra redujo puestos en una empresa conjunta de IA que formó con Accenture, y parte de ese trabajo pasó a India.
Reuters añade que otras firmas australianas también redujeron su plantilla local mientras amplían operaciones en India, Filipinas y Vietnam, aunque en sus anuncios no mencionaron la IA.
Los sindicatos sostienen que el trabajo se pierde

Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they’re no impulse buy.
These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered.
Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn’t told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea.

/plan und /goal nutzen
Im Planmodus werden dir bei ChatGPT laut Renate gezielt Rückfragen gestellt. Darauf basierend entsteht dann ein Plan. Im Vergleich mit einem einfachen Prompt seien die Fragen im Planmodus laut Renate direkt fokussierter.
Aktivierst du den Zielmodus, beschreibst du ChatGPT oder Claude lediglich dein Ziel, inklusiv der beschreibenden Kriterien. Die KI arbeitet dann auf dieses Ergebniss hin, auch über mehrere Schritte. In ChatGPT waren die Modi wie /study zum lernen bisher auch über die Vorauswahl erreichbar, das gelingt allerdings aktuell nicht.
Am einfachsten ist es dabei, diese Chatvorgabe mit /plan und /goal anzufordern. Das funktioniert laut Renate Tool-übergreifend. Selbstläufer sind die Modi jedoch nicht. Así, si la comunidad no ha realizado reclamaciones dentro del plazo legal, puede perder el derecho a exigirlas, pero para ello hay que comprobar dos cosas: cuándo vencieron los recibos y si existió algún tipo de reclamación.
Como recoge El Español en su información sobre las cuotas comunitarias, el Tribunal Supremo confirmó en varias sentencias que el plazo pasa de 15 años a solo 5. De esta forma, el tiempo anterior baja una década y la clave está en que esas cuotas ahora tienen su propia regulación al considerarse pagos periódicos.
Así, el artículo 1966.3 del Código Civil establece 5 años para reclamar cantidades que se deban abonar anualmente o en periodos más cortos. El Supremo reiteró esta interpretación en varias resoluciones, pero hay un detalle importante: el plazo se puede interrumpir si la comunidad reclama la deuda judicial o extrajudicialmente, o si el propio propietario la reconoce. Por eso, no basta con que un recibo tenga más de 5 años para considerarlo prescrito.
A todo esto debemos sumar que la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal obliga a los propietarios a contribuir a los gastos generales del edificio entre los que se incluyen, por ejemplo, servicios y cargas comunes. articles.title: The Memory Challenge Of Physical AI
articles.summary:
Right-size the memory hierarchy around the device’s data streams, reuse patterns, latency requirements, and operating constraints.
Most AI hardware conversations start with compute, which is understandable since accelerators are visible, easy to compare, and often tied to headline performance metrics. Physical AI broadens that conversation by placing greater emphasis on how compute, memory, and data movement work together under real-world operating constraints. For intelligent systems that must see, interpret, decide, and act in the physical world in real time, it’s critical that the right data reaches the right engine at the right time.
As a result, data movement has become an increasingly important consideration when architecting physical AI systems. A physical AI device may simultaneously handle sensor streams, model weights, activations, temporary buffers, control loops, and safety functions. If memory access becomes unpredictable, compute engines can stall. Power consumption rises when data is moved too often, and poorly planned buffering can cause latency accumulation that is hard to recover from later.
As physical AI workloads become more complex, architects must now consider how predictably the complete system performs when multiple real-world workloads are active simultaneously.

articles.title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
articles.summary:
One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet’s atmosphere.
Except when we can’t.
On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we’ve been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that’s due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane.
Big changes
TOI-2535 is one of the many stars with exoplanet candidates identified by TESS, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. It’s a K dwarf, meaning it’s somewhat smaller than the Sun. And TESS found signs of a Jupiter-sized planet orbiting it every eight days, an orbit close enough to make TOI-2535b a “hot Jupiter” exoplanet. At that point, there was nothing especially unusual about it.

articles.title: IP Integration Challenges Evolve
articles.summary:
Integration challenges are growing more complex, but the problem is well understood and solutions are emerging.
Key Takeaways:
IP integration is not the most glamorous task in semiconductor design, but it often is one of the most troublesome. At the intersection of block-level verification and system-level interactions, bugs are often very difficult to find.
The creation of the Virtual Socket Interface Alliance (VSIA) in 1996 was, for many, the first time the notion of designing a system by integrating third-party IP blocks became a reality. Its charter was to unify and standardize the way IP was constructed, verified, delivered, and supported. The alliance dissolved in 2008, considering its work to either be complete, or transferring parts of it to other organizations that were more focused on specific pieces of the problem. Eighteen years later, the problem continues to evolve.
The idea was that each company should focus on developing the part of the design that was novel and unique, adding their expertise, and allowing the rest to be developed by domain experts.
“Ten years ago, a design may have had tens of IP blocks,” says Pedro Pires, SOS product manager at Keysight EDA. “Today, a company may have thousands of IPs, dozens of different versions of the same IP, and you want to make sense of all of this. articles.title: Attacker Targets 60,000 GitHub Repositories in Credential Theft Campaign

An attacker has tested stolen access to more than 60,000 GitHub repositories and inserted credential-stealing code in thousands of them, several security firms report.
Aikido Security said the operation, which it calls wfx-loot, began on November 10. It identified roughly 4,800 compromised accounts behind probe pull requests submitted to 61,764 repositories.
The requests were used to establish whether the stolen access permitted changes to a repository. “The pull request does nothing by itself,” StepSecurity explained, noting that malware was subsequently deployed in repositories where the permissions and configuration allowed it.
Aikido found signs that the stealer ran in more than 1,800 repositories. SafeDep separately counted 8,093 public repositories that received malicious commits, a figure that does not necessarily indicate successful execution.
“The attacker does not exploit a bug in GitHub Actions,” StepSecurity noted. The intruder instead relies on valid tokens belonging to developer and bot accounts.
The attacker placed the malware in existing or new GitHub Actions workflows, shell scripts run by CI systems, and npm installation hooks. The npm method also poses a risk to developers who install dependencies while the malicious changes are present.

“Clinicians should be prepared to encounter increasing numbers of patients presenting with the long-term effects of AAS exposure, including cardiomyopathy, atherosclerotic disease, and anabolic steroid–induced hypogonadism.”

articles.summary:
Cuando el disco duro principal empieza a quedarse sin espacio, solemos buscar qué carpetas del sistema están devorando nuestros gigas. Y es que, si revisamos a fondo la partición del sistema, no es raro encontrarse con que la carpeta WinSxS ha ido creciendo con el paso de las semanas hasta ocupar 10 GB, 12 GB o incluso más de 20 GB sin que nos hayamos dado cuenta.
El almacén del sistema. WinSxS funciona como un repositorio interno de componentes de Microsoft. Su función principal es la de conservar versiones paralelas de diferentes archivos esenciales y librerías DLL para evitar conflictos de compatibilidad, y permitir recuperar versiones anteriores tras cada actualización. El sistema una tarea automática para hacer limpieza llamada StartComponentCleanup, pero no se activa hasta que pasan 30 días enteros tras una actualización, pero si necesitas espacio urgentemente puedes lanzarlo manualmente.
Comprobar el peso real. Muchos de los archivos que residen dentro de WinSxS están vinculados con la carpeta System32, lo que provoca que las propiedades convencionales de Windows Explorer muestren un cálculo distorsionado del espacio. Para salir de dudas y comprobar exactamente cuánto almacenamiento puedes recuperar, basta con abrir PowerShell o el Símbolo del sistema con permisos de administrador y ejecutar el siguiente comando:
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore

articles.title: Your Endpoint Management Platform Could Be Your Biggest Security Risk
articles.summary:
Author: Gene Moody, Field CTO at Action1
Endpoint management platforms have become essential in modern IT operations and enterprise security. They allow administrators to deploy patches, install software, execute scripts, enforce configurations, and remotely manage thousands of devices from a centralized system.
Without these types of systems, maintaining consistent security across large environments would be extremely difficult and labor-intensive.
However, the administrative authority that makes these platforms valuable also makes them very attractive targets for attackers. An endpoint management platform already has established and approved communication channels, elevated permissions, and trusted relationships with the devices it manages.
Any attacker who gains control of that infrastructure will be able to use those existing capabilities to distribute malware, execute malicious commands, disable security controls, or disrupt operations across an entire organization. All with the same level of authority as the real admin.
The same capabilities that allow an administrator to secure thousands of endpoints can allow an attacker to compromise them.
When trusted management infrastructure is compromised

articles.title: Designing Edge AI SoCs At Near-Threshold: Why Foundation IP Can Help You Break Down The Power Wall
articles.summary:
Traditional voltage scaling is no longer sufficient to deliver real-time performance within tight energy and thermal limits.
Lowering operating voltage is a key to SoC power optimization. In advanced FinFET processes at ~0.4–0.5V, it can also start to become a design risk. As edge AI pushes inference closer to endpoints, edge-AI SoCs must deliver real-time performance within tight energy and thermal limits. Traditional voltage scaling is no longer sufficient.
SoC designs are shifting towards much more extensive use of near-threshold operation to achieve step-function improvements in performance per watt. But this shift fundamentally changes how chips behave: delays increase non-linearly, variability grows significantly, and underpinning predictable operation becomes a critical enabler to minimizing power.
Design success in this operating regime depends heavily on the underlying quality, modeling accuracy, and integration of Foundation IP with EDA flows and silicon validation. Embedded memories, logic libraries, and I/Os must be selected carefully and any targeted optimization carried out and fully validated at an early stage—not treated as a possible downstream option.
Every SoC designer understands that lowering supply voltage reduces energy—but at near threshold voltages, it changes transistor behavior and challenges traditional design assumptions.

articles.title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments
articles.summary:
In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed it has replaced Argo CD with its own GitOps engine. This new system deploys applications across over 250 Kubernetes clusters. It supports more than 4,000 services and manages over 100,000 deployments each week. According to a post, deployment infrastructure failures fell from 925 to 63 despite a 3.7x increase in deployment volume. The median time to detect and conclude a failed deployment dropped from 16.1 to 2.45 minutes.
LinkedIn started with one Argo CD instance per cluster, a topology it chose because Argo CD already managed its cluster add-ons that way. Clusters run up to 5,000 nodes each. A central deployment orchestrator spawned an ephemeral pod per deployment, with Argo CD hidden behind it. The team lists seven problems that emerged at scale. Argo CD doesn't have an observedGeneration, so you can't link sync and health status to a specific deployment. LinkedIn created a Lua health check that uses a tracking annotation to address this. A Synced and Healthy application could also resolve to an unintended revision when stale repo-server cache entries were used.
Two of the issues were architectural. Argo CD maintains one watch per group-version-resource across Applications. LinkedIn’s clusters have low resource-type diversity. This means etcd churn from one app can slow syncs for all apps. In one test, sync took under 3 minutes on a cluster with 60,000 pods and over 10 minutes with more than 80,000. articles.title: EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act takes aim at Duolingo streaks, autoplay, and manipulative apps
articles.summary:
In brief: Plenty of apps work hard to retain users, whether it's a pop-up claiming only two items are left or even something like a Duolingo streak you're scared to break. On Wednesday, the European Commission proposed a Digital Fairness Act that would outlaw many of those manipulative "dark patterns." Surprisingly, it doesn't stop at protecting kids. Adults would get to switch off addictive features like autoplay and streaks, too.
That off switch could reach well beyond social media. As WIRED notes, it would cover the daily streaks in apps like Strava and Duolingo. That could sting, since streaks are how those apps keep people coming back. Duolingo once wrote that a new streak animation alone made brand-new learners 1.7% more likely to stick around for a week.
Until now, Brussels could only really chase these designs on online platforms through the Digital Services Act. Last Friday, it accused TikTok of trapping users in "rabbit holes" through its For You feed, months after flagging the app's infinite scroll and autoplay. Its proposed Kids Act targets addictive design too, but only for children.
Beyond addictive features, the new act also names specific dark patterns. Fake claims that a product is almost sold out would be banned, along with opt-out buttons worded to make you feel bad for declining.
Subscriptions get a cleanup as well. Free trials couldn't roll into a paid plan without your active approval. Canceling one would have to be easy, too. If something still goes wro…

Gootloader is a malware loader active since 2020, StealC is an infostealer that helps exfiltrate credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and other sensitive information from victims' devices, and CastleRAT is a remote access trojan that surfaced last year. All three malware families have been used by various cybercriminal operations, including ransomware gangs.
The joint action is part of Operation Endgame, an international law enforcement effort targeting cybercrime and "cybercrime-as-a-service" networks. Together with private partners who helped identify, take down, seize, and block infrastructure tied to the three malware operations, the authorities seized 257 domains and 235 servers.

Fin août, le télescope Nancy Grace Roman a pris son envol avec la mission de percer les mystères de la matière noire. Mais dans la foulée, le Swift, l’observatoire qui scrutait les sursauts gamma, a poursuivi sa chute pour venir s’abîmer dans l’atmosphère début novembre. Quant au vénérable Hubble, la NASA vient de lancer un appel au secteur privé pour tenter de lui offrir une seconde vie car il se dirige, lui aussi, vers sa destruction. Mais pas de panique : l’agence spatiale prépare la relève.
Cartographie du ciel

articles.title: Coraltalk wants universities to stop chasing AI cheaters and start measuring learning | BetaKit

“Show your work” is an instruction known to just about anyone who has gone to school.
With generative AI now capable of producing entire assignments, universities have good reason to revisit that old classroom principle. Asking students to explain their reasoning can help instructors establish what they’ve actually learned, but in a large university class, that’s easier said than done.
Suppose a university professor wanted to sit down with each of their 75 students and ask them a few questions about their latest assignment. If they were to dedicate 15 minutes per student, the exercise would take close to 20 hours, before accounting for preparation, scheduling, or grading. Melissa Morgan, co-founder and CEO of Toronto-based EdTech startup Coraltalk, believes technology could make these kinds of assessments achievable on a much larger scale.
“A detector estimates whether text may have been produced by AI,” Morgan said. “It cannot tell a professor whether the student understands the argument, could explain a decision, or would know what to do if the facts changed.”
Coraltalk is using conversational AI to bring oral examinations into the digital age. Instructors provide the platform with course materials, assignments, and grading criteria, which the software uses to question students about their work. As students respond, the AI asks follow-up questions to probe their understanding.
A new take on an old-school approach

Whoop already has a social feature, Teams, which a little more than half its customers use, according to the company. But Teams is built around groups and leaderboards, and everyone in a group sees everyone else’s information. Humans is meant to be more intimate. articles.title: Author Q+A: finprim is a Case for One Financial Validation Library in TypeScript
articles.summary:
finprim, which is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library that puts IBAN, BIC, card, sort code, VAT, routing number and loan calculations behind one API, has published its fifth release, 0.1.4. The repository has 81 stars.
InfoQ asked author Oluwatosin Adelaja what pushed him to build it, and where he wants it to stop.
InfoQ: What pushed you to build finprim?
Adelaja: Honestly, it came from doing the same work too many times. At Sprint Technology Solutions we had several products, and each one ended up with its own copy of the same financial validation, sort code checks in one place, IBAN formatting in another, card validation somewhere else, all written slightly differently by whoever got there first.
The moment it really landed for me was on a payout flow. We had account and sort code validation on the web side, and then the mobile app needed the same thing. Rather than share it, the validation got rewritten for mobile, and the two copies drifted. One of them was a little stricter than the other, so a bank detail that the web form accepted would get rejected on mobile, and we had people re-entering details that were actually fine. It took longer than it should have to track down, because nobody thinks to check whether two "identical" validators are actually identical. The fix was easy once we found it, but the real problem was that there were two of them at all.

articles.title: Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
articles.summary:
Apache has patched a critical HTTP Server vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), following independent discoveries by Anthropic and Google researchers.
Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, the flaw affects Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The issue was addressed on November 11 with the release of version 2.4.71. It resides in mod_http2, the module responsible for handling HTTP/2 traffic.
The vulnerability involves a race condition in which multiple threads improperly access shared resources, potentially corrupting server memory.
According to Red Hat, an attacker could exploit the issue remotely without authentication to execute arbitrary commands and gain control of the server process. Red Hat assigned the vulnerability a CVSS score of 9.8 and explained that “only servers that have HTTP/2 enabled are affected; servers configured to serve only HTTP/1.1 are not vulnerable.”
Apache credited Anthropic’s OSS Scanner with reporting the flaw on October 26. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research independently reported the same vulnerability on November 3.
Cloud security firm Wiz reported that 64% of cloud environments in its data contained resources running affected Apache versions, while 51% had publicly exposed instances. The company cautioned that these figures do not account for server configuration, so they do not necessarily represent exploitable installations.

What just happened? Cheap home internet isn't much use if it slows to a crawl a few days into the month. New York says that's exactly what T-Mobile was offering low-income households, imposing a 50GB monthly cap before slashing download speeds to under 1 Mbps. The carrier has now agreed to remove the restriction after state investigators found it violated the Affordable Broadband Act.
Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James announced the agreement on November 9. The law requires qualifying households to be offered broadband costing $15 per month with download speeds of at least 25 Mbps, or $20 for at least 200 Mbps. Those prices include taxes and equipment fees.
The agreement covers home broadband delivered over T-Mobile's cellular network, rather than its mobile phone plans. Customers shouldn't expect the settlement to change their handset data allowances.
T-Mobile's $15 fixed wireless plan came with a fairly big catch. According to the signed settlement, customers who used 50GB saw their maximum download speed fall from 25 Mbps to just 600 Kbps, a reduction of 97.6%. State officials estimate a typical customer could burn through the allowance in about four days, which isn't what you'd call a month's worth of usable broadband.

articles.title: The death of the 14-day patch: Surviving machine-speed vulnerability discovery
articles.summary:
The death of the 14-day patch: Surviving machine-speed vulnerability discovery
For decades, enterprise vulnerability management ran on human time: A security researcher manually dissected a binary, traced execution paths, built a proof of concept, and filed a coordinated disclosure. Engineering leads evaluated the CVSS score and prioritized the fi before working it into an upcoming sprint schedule. Then, finally, they shipped the update.
That deliberate cadence is a thing of the past.
In the first nine months of 2026, publishers recorded 75,242 CVEs, representing roughly 20% of all vulnerabilities published since the CVE program was established in 1999.
The acceleration is steepening: according to the Cyber Strategy Institute, nearly 38,000 of those flaws surfaced in Q3 alone.
“The pace of vulnerability discovery has outpaced the human capacity to remediate it. Engineering organizations face a stark operational reality: the traditional two-week patch cycle is dead.”
The pace of vulnerability discovery has outpaced the human capacity to remediate it. Engineering organizations face a stark operational reality: the traditional two-week patch cycle is dead.
Why vulnerabilities exploded in 2026
This surge is not caused by developers writing worse code. It is the direct result of vulnerability hunting transforming from an artisan craft into an autonomous, distributed compute problem.

articles.title: Los centros de datos de IA castigan con facturas hasta un 76% más altas a los hogares rurales y de menores ingresos en Estados Unidos
articles.summary:
Cada vez que una empresa tecnológica instala un nuevo centro de datos en Estados Unidos, alguien más paga la cuenta. Ese alguien, según un estudio publicado esta semana en la revista científica Nature Energy, suele ser un hogar rural de bajos ingresos ubicado a cientos de kilómetros del servidor más cercano.
El mecanismo por el que la expansión de la inteligencia artificial traslada sus costos energéticos a los consumidores más vulnerables es el centro del análisis elaborado por investigadores de la Universidad de Cornell.
El trabajo examinó cuatro de las principales redes eléctricas del país entre 2020 y 2025, junto con datos de 4.000 centros de datos existentes y en proyecto. En ese período, el gasto total en infraestructura eléctrica saltó de USD 2.000 millones a USD 34.200 millones.
Los centros de datos generaron USD 8.250 millones de esos costos, pero se les facturó apenas USD 3.000 millones. Los usuarios residenciales causaron USD 3.500 millones y terminaron pagando más de USD 16.000 millones.
Un problema estructural con décadas de antigüedad
El desequilibrio tiene un origen estructural. Las fórmulas que rigen la distribución de costos en las redes eléctricas fueron diseñadas para dividir los gastos según el consumo histórico, no según el crecimiento nuevo.
Eso hace que los hogares absorban buena parte del costo de expandir la infraestructura que los centros de datos necesitan para operar.

articles.title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
articles.summary:
Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (also known as Nightmare Eclipse) has released a new Windows zero-day exploit that can let attackers gain SYSTEM privileges.
Named SignDrop, it exploits mitigations Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to defend against authentication attacks targeting vulnerabilities in the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver. Naceri added that attacks exploiting CLFS vulnerabilities dropped sharply after the mitigation, but that Microsoft's mitigation itself introduced this new vulnerability.
According to Naceri, the flaw is in how CLFS handles creating the authentication file (".cnpf") when it creates a new log file. He said that CLFS enforces access checks correctly at the start, but the logic can be abused if a different, privileged process later opens the log file.
He also added that privileged processes such as Windows Defender can be forced to open the files, so the authentication file gets created with SYSTEM privileges, and CLFS creates it with the original file's access permissions.
Naceri noted that Microsoft implemented the mitigation properly but that "the logic allows abuse" and said the technique works against any antimalware engine's self-defense (tamper protection), because the file-creation request appears to come from the engine's own legitimate process.

articles.title: The Semiconductor Singularity: When AI Starts Accelerating The Silicon That Accelerates AI
articles.summary:
Use evidence from silicon to improve the tools and decisions that create the next generation of hardware.
AI is entering the inner loop of semiconductor engineering by reducing the effort required to develop software, operate software tools and carry out engineering analysis.
Ray Kurzweil described the broader pattern as the Law of Accelerating Returns: accumulated technical capability helps create the next computing paradigm. In my recent white paper, The semiconductor singularity: Accelerating IC innovation with AI, I applied that idea to semiconductor engineering. Better computing improves the tools used to design and manufacture semiconductors, and those tools help create the next generation of computing.
Figure 1 places that loop in the longer history of computing. The technologies change, but each generation contributes tools, knowledge and capacity that help create its successor.
Fig. 1: Successive computing paradigms have built the technical capacity used to create the next generation.
Progress in semiconductor engineering never follows a smooth exponential curve. It advances when a bottleneck is overcome sufficiently for engineers to try something that previously cost too much money, time, computation or organizational effort.

articles.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's successor | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” he wrote.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company, but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday, suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs.
Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess.
“Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does.

articles.title: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn
articles.summary:
We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird’s blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers, and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy.
As previously reported, Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He’s been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year.
The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “Planet Claire” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn. Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on “raygun,” of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird.

articles.title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs

Google Cloud has open-sourced TPU Sync, a native C++ library that moves KV cache blocks and model weights between TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network. GCP also announced the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max systems, the project targets two workloads where accelerators often wait on data: long-context and disaggregated LLM serving, and reinforcement learning loops that push updated weights from trainers to rollout samplers.
For prefill/decode disaggregation, Google says median KV transfer latency for Qwen3 235B fell from several seconds to about 230 ms, with average TTFT reductions of 60% for that model and 90% for a 480B model at low concurrency. For prefix caching, it reports up to 90% lower average TTFT on 64K-context workloads.
Developers get Python wheels for JAX and PyTorch, with KV cache manager, KV store, and weight synchronizer APIs. TPU Sync acts as the KV connector for vLLM-TorchTPU through vLLM's KVConnector interface, as the disaggregation and hierarchical-cache backend for SGLang-TorchTPU, and pairs with llm-d 1.0 on GKE for prefix-cache-aware routing. The RL weight-sync module for Pathways and multi-controller JAX is experimental. The GitHub repository, which absorbed the earlier TPU Raiden codebase, warns that APIs are changing rapidly and that only development builds are on PyPI, and recommends pinning to its last-known-good commit. articles.summary:
A critical vulnerability in the HTTP/2 module of Apache HTTP Server could be exploited by an unauthenticated attacker to obtain remote code execution (RCE).
The Apache Software Foundation has fixed the issue, now tracked as CVE-2026-119618, but a significant number of servers are vulnerable and reachable over the public internet.
Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner and Google Cloud’s Vulnerability Research teams, the vulnerability is a race condition in the mod_http2 module that can corrupt heap memory.
An attacker successfully exploiting it could run code with the web server process’s privileges in HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, and standalone mod_h2 version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
Apache describes the problem as “Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 in assign_headers() can lead to RCE.”
Apache HTTP Server is a free and open-source software that handles requests from web browsers and serves pages, images, and other website content. It is a widely used tool estimated to back roughly one out of five websites.
According to telemetry data from cloud security company Wiz, 64% of the cloud environments have vulnerable resources, and roughly half of them have publicly exposed instances.
However, the numbers do not account for server configuration, which requires HTTP/2 to be enabled (default is off).

…the routine decisions that AI applications make thousands of times a day, with lower costs and faster response times than traditional generative models.

articles.title: Beyond Bandwidth: AI Inference Is Reshaping The Memory Wall
articles.summary:
Longer contexts, higher concurrency, multimodal models, and AI agents will continue changing where memory pressure appears.
AI infrastructure has spent the past several years in a race for compute. More accelerators, larger heterogeneous clusters, and higher peak performance have enabled increasingly capable models. As AI moves into large-scale deployment, infrastructure must support more users, larger models, longer context windows, and more complex applications. Performance still matters, but so do latency, power, utilization, predictability, and cost per inference.
The challenge extends beyond bandwidth. AI systems must balance memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, power, data movement, utilization, and cost. Improving one dimension can create pressure elsewhere. The key-value (KV) cache illustrates this trade-off. KV cache reduces repeated computation during generative AI inference, but requires the system to retain and repeatedly access growing amounts of data. As context lengths and concurrent requests increase, the trade-off becomes more significant.
The result is not simply another memory bottleneck. It is a coordination problem across compute, memory, interconnect, and software. Adding capacity or bandwidth helps only if the system can place, move, and retrieve data without allowing latency, congestion, power, or complexity to erase the benefit.

Google has yet to share specs, prices or ship dates for either new system.
Google's eighth-generation TPU family has now expanded further. Back in April, the company announced TPU 8t for training AI models and TPU 8i for general-purpose inference workloads. Google has now introduced TPU 8tx, built on the same silicon as the previously announced 8t, for confidential, hardware-isolated inference aimed at regulated enterprises and governments, and TPU 8i Max, which combines two 8i chips on one package for long-context agentic work.
TPU 8tx swaps the Arm-based Axion hosts of the 8t and 8i for a 5th Gen AMD EPYC CPU, adopting a Boardfly network, and the 8i Max doubles the compute, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth of the original 8i. The original split, the TPU 8t and 8i, made natural sense. The 8t targets large-scale training, while the 8i leans toward low-latency inference and reasoning. TPUs have become a fast-growing business, with the company claiming nearly 100 customers, including Meta’s recent move to TPUs. The more modular approach is flexible and can deliver specialized systems “in a matter of months rather than years,” helping that popularity along.

articles.summary:
74 Millionen Geräte betroffen: Warum viele den Wechsel von Windows 10 hinauszögern
Der offizielle Support für Windows 10 hat im Oktober 2025 geendet. Geräte mit diesem veralteten Betriebssystem erhalten keine Updates mehr und sind somit anfälliger für Sicherheitsbedrohungen. Trotzdem haben viele Nutzer:innen den Wechsel zu Windows 11 lange aufgeschoben. Einer der Gründe ist, dass das Upgrade bei vielen aus technischen Gründen nicht möglich ist. Dadurch sind Millionen Computer praktisch unbrauchbar geworden, obwohl sie weiterhin einwandfrei funktionieren. Im Auftrag von Refurbed hat Fraunhofer Austria jetzt im Rahmen einer Studie ermittelt, wie viele Geräte das in Europa konkret betrifft.
Millionen Computer können nicht wechseln
Die aktuelle Windows-Version setzt bestimmte Hardwarevoraussetzungen voraus, darunter TPM 2.0, Secure Boot und eine unterstützte Prozessorgeneration. Laut der Fraunhofer-Analyse können im gewerblichen Bereich nur rund 2,8 Prozent der Windows-10-Geräte technisch nicht auf das neue Betriebssystem wechseln. Die Migration wird hier vor allem durch langsame Beschaffungszyklen, Testphasen und knappe IT-Ressourcen verzögert. Im privaten Bereich fällt der Anteil der technisch inkompatiblen Geräte dagegen deutlich höher aus.

Chainguard defends its choice to break the PHP security embargo: “We own the decision.”
At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 this week, Chainguard co-founder and CTO Matt Moore defended the company’s decision to release patched PHP images before an agreed-upon embargo with other partners had lifted.
When Chainguard shipped patched PHP container images more than six hours ahead of an October 21 coordinated security release, PHP’s maintainers accused the company of giving attackers a head start. Chainguard argues attackers already had one.
In an interview with The New Stack, Moore said, “We own the decision that we chose to do it. Nobody could force us to do it — but we did not do it in a vacuum.” He also described, in discussions with TNS, other participants in the embargo and security vendors’ reports of activity targeting the vulnerabilities before Chainguard released its images.
Chainguard was not saying that they patched it faster so they shipped it first. According to Moore, Chainguard believed attackers could already exploit the bugs, or were at least close to figuring out how — or were trying to figure it out.
The two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state), collectively known as PHP2Shell, were serious memory-management and error-handling flaws. Under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker could execute code on a PHP server.

articles.title: Nigerians can pay without cards or transfers, yet remain completely unaware
articles.summary:
The next time a point-of-sale (PoS) agent asks for a bank card, inserting it may not be necessary. Some Nigerian cards can already complete transactions with a single tap.
TechCabal tested this at a local PoS merchant. Using a Verve debit card issued through ALAT, the digital banking platform of tier-2 Nigerian lender Wema Bank, the team held the card near the terminal instead of inserting it. The machine recognised the card, requested a PIN, and dispensed ₦1,500 ($1.11) from the ₦1,600 ($1.19) transaction, which included a ₦100 ($0.074) merchant fee. The cash withdrawal went through without the card being inserted into the machine.
It was a small transaction, but it demonstrated a payment capability already available on some Nigerian cards and PoS terminals, yet still unfamiliar to many consumers.
The feature is easier to spot than it may seem. Look for a small contactless symbol on the card or PoS terminal: four curved lines that resemble radio waves. The symbol is often mistaken for the Wi-Fi logo, but it signals something different. On a card, it means the card can make contactless payments; on a terminal, it means the machine can accept them. The tap works through Near Field Communication (NFC), a technology that lets devices exchange data when they are close to each other.
Contactless payments are not new to Nigeria. In May 2015, Unified Payments, a Nigerian payment processing company, introduced a Near Field Communication (NFC) payment solution.
